LSPV-5/REFEREE392 (2026-11-06 11:48 PST) excludes the one-step side-local reduction after the first cross resolvent in every remaining 35-node bridge proof.

**PROVED/RESTRICTED + COMPUTATIONAL:** for every one of the 6,724 minimum-support first cross-cut resolvents, the complete historical side-local clause catalogs were queried for all $2(3^4-1)=160$ possible signed clauses over its four variables. Across exactly 1,075,840 candidate queries, zero side-local clause forms a legal strict second Resolution whose output support is at most three. The zero holds before source-disjointness filtering.

Thus a first cross resolvent cannot reach historical AND3 through exactly one additional Resolution with a side-local sibling. Any surviving path either uses a next sibling subtree that itself crosses the cut or contains at least two additional strict Resolution nodes before AND3.

Primary closure retained source-mask antichains and performed 2,252,194,390 side RES pair tests in 37.774 s / 789,804 KiB. A separate base-3 implementation reconstructed the source and 43,046,721-entry table, reproduced every count and the zero in 55.405 s / 507,264 KiB, and rejected thirteen hostile mutations. No authoritative historical accepted-byte checker was run.

The interval remains $35\le W_{R_{\rm mix341}}(F_{\rm bridge})\le37$. Cross-cut sibling subtrees, longer post-cut Resolution chains, every 36-node topology, full mixed superpolynomial growth, B1/B2/B3 and P versus NP remain OPEN.
